newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Mandela to assist U.N. over East Timor.
newsitem.headline: Mandela to assist U.N. over East Timor.

text.p: South African President Nelson Mandela said on Friday he would assist the United Nations in finding a solution for East Timor rather than directly negotiating in the dispute over the Pacific territory.
Mandela met East Timor exile Jose Ramos Horta, a fellow recipient of the Nobel Peace Prize, in Pretoria on Friday and said he had briefed him on his recent state visit to Indonesia.
"It must not be regarded that I am now deciding to negotiate with regard to East Timor," Mandela told a news conference afterwards.
"I am doing this just as an aide to the secretary general of the United Nations (Kofi Annan), for whom we have the highest regard.
"We would like to assist him in the difficult task that is facing him," Mandela said.
The former Portuguese colony of East Timor was annexed by Indonesia in 1976, a year after Portugal pulled out. Up to 200,000 people are believed to have died in the violent takeover.
The Indonesian move has never been recognised by the United Nations which continues to regard Lisbon as the territory's legal administrator.
During his visit to Jakarta, Mandela saw Indonesia's best-known political prisoner, Xanana Gusmao, who is serving a 20-year sentence for resisting Indonesian rule.
Ramos Horta is Gusmao's spokesman in exile.
Mandela said because of the sensitivity of the issue, he preferred not to discuss details of the Horta meeting.
"If discussion is going to succeed, the element of confidentiality must be maintained," Mandela said.
Horta said Mandela's efforts would make a difference.

"We reiterated to the President our deepest respect for the president, his moral authority and whatever South Africa can contribute in enhancing the mandate of the Secretary General who is doing an outstanding job in dialogue between Portugal, Indonesia and ourselves," he said.
"I believe personally that President Mandela can really make a difference in this entire process," he added.
Friday's meeting was the second between Mandela and Ramos Horta. The two men met in Johannesburg last September shortly before the award of the Nobel prize.
